newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador GDP up 2.0 pct in '96 -Central Bank source.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador GDP up 2.0 pct in '96 -Central Bank source.

text.p: Ecuador's gross domestic product grew 2.0 percent in 1996, down from 2.4 percent growth in 1995, a top Central Bank source said Friday.
The source, who requested anonymity, told Reuters political uncertainty was partly responsible for the lower rate of growth.
Abdala Bucaram was elected president in July, but Congress removed him in February 1997 and elected Fabian Alarcon as interim president until August 1998.
The government forecast annual growth of 3.5 percent in 1997 and 4.0 percent in 1998.
In 1994, Ecuadorean GDP grew by 4.3 percent.

Growth in 1996 was led by the banking sector, up 9.8 percent, followed by 8.8 percent growth for other financial services. Trade grew by 4.5 percent, agriculture by 3.5 percent and manufacturing by 3.3 percent.
The petroleum sector contracted 1.9 percent in the same period, while government services were off 0.9 percent.
In the last quarter of 1996, Ecuador's GDP grew 1.4 percent, up from 0.2 percent growth registered in the same period of 1995.
